text:
An old fisherman lived on the coast. Every day, he threw his net into the sea, and every day it came back almost empty. He was tired and poor, and he was losing hope.

One evening, he sat on the beach and spoke to himself. “Maybe I should stop. The sea doesn’t want to give me fish anymore.”

A young boy was sitting nearby and heard him. “Excuse me, sir,” he said. “Why do you only fish near the rocks?”

“Because I have always fished here,” said the old man. “My father did it, and his father too.”

“But the other fishermen go to the north bay,” said the boy. “My uncle caught twenty fish there yesterday.”

The old man was silent. He had never thought about that. For forty years, he had used the same place and the same method, and he had expected different results.

The next morning, he took his boat to the north bay. It was frightening at first because the water was deep and unfamiliar. But when he pulled up his net, it was heavy and full of silver fish.

He laughed out loud. “Forty years,” he said to the sea. “Why did I wait so long?”

Moral: If you want different results, try something different.

quiz.q: The old fisherman always fished near the rocks.
The boy told him to stop fishing.
Where did the other fishermen go?
What happened in the north bay?
o: His net was heavy and full of fish

quiz.q: If you want different results, try something ___.
